headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: aci can expose CRM/email data to unstructured’s file-processing pipeline, while shared writes and broad egress create conflict and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can pass content through MCP/direct function calls, and unstructured reads documents from files; if aci forwards untrusted text into unstructured, prompt-like instructions embedded in documents could influence downstream handling. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF aci forwards document text or email content into unstructured without sanitization
IF unstructured output is later reinterpreted as instructions by aci or a downstream agent
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction-stripping preprocessor
Require human review of any extracted directives before execution
Tag all cross-agent payloads with provenance metadata
Restrict aci to passing only whitelisted fields to unstructured
requires-engineering: implement content provenance enforcement in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; unstructured reads filesystem documents and can write outputs. If sensitive aci data is written into shared files or passed for parsing, unstructured may process and expose it through its outputs or logs. The pairwise leakage path is credible despite no direct shared-workspace proof.
conditions: IF aci exports CRM/email/support records into files consumed by unstructured
IF unstructured outputs are stored in a shared location accessible to other systems
mitigations: Keep sensitive aci outputs out of shared directories
Use per-agent encrypted workspaces
Disable unnecessary logging for parsed documents
Review and redact CRM/email fields before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce access controls between agent workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API/network actions, while unstructured can read and write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. If both operate on the same directory or artifacts, concurrent writes and state corruption are plausible, and the profiles do not show locking or isolation between them.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or git-tracked workspace
IF aci and unstructured run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Make one agent read-only for shared artifacts
Run unstructured in its container with no shared mount
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions, and unstructured can transform documents into downstream text. If aci’s extracted content is fed into unstructured and then reused by aci or another workflow without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect records or actions. The pair does not document a built-in validation step, so the risk is real but not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF unstructured output is treated as authoritative by aci or a downstream automation
IF extracted text is used to create or modify CRM/email/calendar records without review
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any write action
Require confidence thresholds for extracted fields
Compare extracted values against source documents
Limit automation to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, and customer support data, which may include regulated personal data, while unstructured processes documents and exposes a privacy-policy endpoint but no explicit residency or retention guarantees here. If EU or sensitive customer data flows from aci into unstructured’s document pipeline, policy mismatch is plausible; the profiles do not prove a violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from aci is sent into unstructured for processing
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not documented in either profile
mitigations: Classify data before handoff
Block regulated fields from document pipelines
Review vendor privacy and retention terms
Keep sensitive records in a separate tenant
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
